question_prompt: rative drug therapy management (CDTM) agreement with TWO supervising physicians. The agreement authorizes patient-specific prescribing. topic: Automated pickup APS versus robotic PPA: schedule restrictions, cold products, and mixed-lot recall controls

It has no pharmacy-services authorization on the facility license and no separate M.G.L. c.94C §9(e) authorization to dispense take-home controlled substances. A clinic practitioner legally authorized to prescribe issues several orders. Which proposed dispensing fits 105 CMR 722.091?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Fill an otherwise lawful noncontrolled prescription for a current clinic employee pursuant to the clinic's employee health policy.
citation: 105 CMR 722.020 (Clinic Pharmacy, Clinic Employee, Clinic Patient); 105 CMR 722.091(A)–(B) (effective Sept. 27, 2024)

topic: FDA patient package inserts for contraceptives and estrogen products versus voluntary labeling
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy handles FDA-regulated patient labeling. It dispenses outpatient oral contraceptives and prescription estrogen products, plus a third medication whose FDA-approved Patient Information leaflet is voluntary under federal regulations. No acute-care or long-term-care institutional schedule applies. Which statements about Patient Package Inserts (PPIs) are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: A required oral-contraceptive PPI must accompany each outpatient package dispensed to the patient or appropriate agent. | Prescription estrogen products covered by 21 CFR 310.515 generally require a PPI to accompany dispensing; oral contraceptives with estrogen and progestogen are instead addressed under §310.501.
citation: 21 CFR 310.501(a),(b)(2); 21 CFR 310.515(a),(b),(e); FDA Patient Labeling Resources (mandatory versus voluntary PPIs)

topic: Brand and generic schedule identification: pregabalin Lyrica versus lisdexamfetamine Vyvanse
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist receives valid prescriptions for Lyrica (pregabalin) capsules and Vyvanse (lisdexamfetamine) capsules. Both prescriptions were written by an authorized prescriber for a legitimate purpose. Which statement correctly identifies both federal and Massachusetts schedules and their basic refill implications?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Lyrica is Schedule V in both systems and may have lawfully authorized refills; Vyvanse is Schedule II in both systems and cannot be refilled.
citation: 21 CFR 1308.15(e)(7) (pregabalin), 1308.12(d)(5) (lisdexamfetamine), 1306.12(a); 105 CMR 700.002(B),(E); 21 CFR 1306.22 (Schedule III–V refills)

topic: Massachusetts nonresident pharmacy license combinations for shipment of sterile and complex nonsterile compounds
question_prompt: Three out-of-state pharmacies want to mail prescriptions to Massachusetts residents. Each holds a valid license in its own state and is otherwise compliant. Pharmacy A ships conventional prescription products; B ships compounded sterile preparations; C ships complex nonsterile compounded preparations. Which Massachusetts licensure statements are correct under 247 CMR 6.02? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: A nonresident pharmacy shipping prescription controlled substances into Massachusetts must hold the Massachusetts nonresident Drug Store Pharmacy license; its home-state license alone does not replace this requirement. | Shipping sterile compounded prescriptions into Massachusetts requires both a Massachusetts nonresident Drug Store Pharmacy license and a Massachusetts nonresident sterile compounding pharmacy license.
citation: 247 CMR 6.02(4)–(6); 247 CMR 6.09 (nonresident pharmacy applications); M.G.L. c.94C §1 Schedule VI definition (247 CMR 6.00 effective Apr. 25, 2025)

topic: Individual pharmacist disclosure: an arrest and an out-of-state disciplinary action
question_prompt: A Massachusetts-licensed pharmacist is arrested in another state for a misdemeanor, before any criminal charge or conviction. In an independent later event, another state's licensing board formally disciplines the pharmacist's professional license. The pharmacist reviews BOTH 247 CMR 20.03 and the grounds for discipline in 247 CMR 10.03. Which reporting approach is BEST supported by the two published regulations?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Report the arrest within 14 calendar days under §20.03(3); report the out-of-state disciplinary action within the 14-calendar-day §20.03(4) period AND meet any independently applicable, shorter seven-business-day §10.03(1)(y)-(z) reporting obligation.
citation: 247 CMR 20.03(3)-(4); 247 CMR 10.03(1)(y)-(aa); Massachusetts Board Mandatory Disclosure Form, revised Dec. 6, 2024; concurrent triggers, not claimed supersession

topic: Hospital DEA registration and unique institutional suffix for otherwise authorized resident prescribers
question_prompt: A Massachusetts hospital has a current DEA hospital registration. A physician resident is legally authorized under Massachusetts law to prescribe the relevant Schedule II drug, but lacks an individual DEA registration. The hospital has verified the resident's authority and may grant use of its registration. Assume any necessary state controlled-substance registration and ePrescribing rules are separately met. Which federal DEA conclusions are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The resident may use the hospital DEA registration while prescribing in the usual course of practice within the resident's hospital employment, if the institution authorizes it and assigns a unique internal suffix. | The hospital must maintain a current roster connecting unique internal codes to prescribers and make the information available to other registrants or law-enforcement agencies on request.
citation: 21 CFR 1301.22(c)(1)–(6); DEA Pharmacist's Manual and DEA Medical Resident Guidance; 21 CFR 1306.04(a); applicable 105 CMR 700 and 721 must also be satisfied

topic: Massachusetts prescription formats: multiple drug products on one record in hospital versus other settings
question_prompt: A practitioner plans to prescribe two different prescription drug products on one record. In one case the prescriptions are issued for community outpatient dispensing; in a separate case they are issued in the hospital setting with clear use and interchange directions for each product. All other requirements are met. Which decision correctly applies 105 CMR 721.050?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Separate records are required for the ordinary outpatient case; the hospital record may include multiple drug products if each has clear directions for use and interchange.
citation: 105 CMR 721.050 (Prescribing More than One Drug Product); 105 CMR 721.020(A),(D) (effective Sept. 27, 2024)

topic: Diphenoxylate/atropine Lomotil Schedule V threshold versus diphenoxylate itself
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist reviews the schedule of FDA-approved Lomotil tablets containing 2.5 mg diphenoxylate hydrochloride and 25 micrograms atropine sulfate per unit. For comparison, the pharmacist also checks the federal schedule of diphenoxylate itself outside this qualifying combination. Assume no separate exception or rescheduling order. Which classification is correct?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The qualifying diphenoxylate/atropine combination is Schedule V in federal and Massachusetts law, while diphenoxylate itself is federally Schedule II.
citation: 21 CFR 1308.15(c)(4) (combination threshold); 21 CFR 1308.12(c)(8) (diphenoxylate); 105 CMR 700.002(B),(E) (Massachusetts corresponding schedules)

topic: USP <797> initial garbing versus media-fill competency: distinct assessments and numbers
question_prompt: A Massachusetts sterile compounding pharmacy trains a new employee for Category 2 compounded sterile preparations (CSPs). The trainee has no previous sterile-compounding qualification. The facility follows the currently official USP <797> requirements and the USP FAQ explanations of §§2.2–2.3. Which procedures are correct BEFORE the employee begins compounding CSPs? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Complete an initial garbing competency with visual observation and gloved fingertip/thumb sampling successfully on at least three separate occasions in succession. | Complete an initial aseptic manipulation competency including a media-fill test and gloved fingertip/thumb sampling after that test.
citation: Current USP <797> §§2.2–2.3 (official Nov. 1, 2023); USP <797> Official FAQ updated Dec. 11, 2023, Q49–50, 57; 247 CMR 9.01(3)

topic: A nationally certified technician's certification lapse while Massachusetts technician license remains active
question_prompt: A Massachusetts community pharmacy has an employee with a current Massachusetts pharmacy technician license whose certification from a Board-approved national certifying body expired yesterday. The pharmacist is reviewing the employee's duties, name badge, and supervisory-ratio roster. Under 247 CMR 8.04(3), which changes or conclusions are required? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The worker remains eligible to perform ordinary licensed pharmacy technician functions under 247 CMR 8.02, assuming the Massachusetts license remains valid. | For the supervisory-ratio calculation the employee must be counted as an ordinary pharmacy technician, not a certified pharmacy technician.

topic: Hospital ED/discharge patient outpatient dispensing: 14-day supply and no hospital refill
question_prompt: A Massachusetts hospital pharmacy receives an otherwise valid prescription for an emergency department patient who has completed treatment and is leaving the hospital. The prescribed medication is routinely stocked by community retail pharmacies and is available in quantities that permit dispensing exactly a 14-day supply. The prescriber orders 30 days plus two refills. No waiver applies. What may the hospital pharmacy dispense under 105 CMR 722.090?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: At most an initial 14-day supply without refills at the hospital pharmacy; the remaining continuing therapy needs an appropriate lawful outpatient dispensing arrangement.
citation: 105 CMR 722.090(A)–(C), especially (B)(1)–(2) (regulation published Sept. 27, 2024; substantive §722.090(B) text dates May 5, 2017)

topic: ePrescribing exemption duties: pharmacist verification versus invalid electronic-to-fax transmissions
question_prompt: A Massachusetts retail pharmacist receives several otherwise authentic prescriptions in November 2026. A prescriber may rely on an enumerated exception from electronic prescribing, but the pharmacist did not personally witness the underlying reason. In another case, a purported electronic prescription arrived only as a fax (not a verified technical failover). Which legal conclusions follow 105 CMR 721.040 and 721.070? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The pharmacist is not required to independently verify that an otherwise valid written or oral prescription falls within a prescriber's ePrescribing exception, though other validity and safety checks remain required. | A properly issued Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription falls under an express state ePrescribing exception, so it need not be transmitted electronically solely because it is a prescription drug.

topic: DEA Schedule II fax-as-original exceptions: LTCF residents, hospice narcotics and ordinary outpatients
question_prompt: cist receives practitioner-signed PAPER Schedule II prescriptions transmitted by fax for three patients: (1) a current long-term care facility resident, (2) a patient in an eligible hospice program whose narcotic prescription bears the required hospice notation, and (3) an ordinary community outpatient with no listed federal fax exception. Assume each paper prescription is otherwise lawful under a Massachusetts ePrescribing exception and meets federal requirements. Which federal dispensing determination is correct?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The fax may serve as the original for the LTCF resident and for the appropriately noted hospice narcotic prescription, but not for the ordinary outpatient's nonexceptional Schedule II prescription.
citation: 21 CFR 1306.11(a),(e)–(g); 21 CFR 1306.05; 105 CMR 721.020(F),721.070(A),(C) (assumed valid MA ePrescribing exception)

topic: USP <797> Category 3 extended BUD: additional sterility testing and ongoing facility requirements
question_prompt: A Massachusetts sterile compounding pharmacy wants to assign a beyond-use date longer than the Category 2 BUD limit to one nonhazardous compounded sterile preparation. It has a compliant cleanroom suite and trained staff but has not implemented Category 3 additional qualifications or sterility testing. Manufacturer component expiration does not limit the proposed date. Which approach is consistent with the currently official USP <797> standard?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Do not assign the extended Category 3 BUD until all additional Category 3 requirements and required testing for that CSP are met; a suitable shorter BUD may be chosen.
citation: Official USP <797> §§14.3–14.4 (revision official Nov. 1, 2023); USP <797> FAQs Dec. 11, 2023, Q12, 174, 182; 247 CMR 9.01(3)

topic: Retail Manager of Record: planned six-week absence and simultaneous management restriction
question_prompt: The Massachusetts pharmacist Manager of Record (MOR) of Retail Pharmacy A plans to be away for six weeks. Before leaving, the MOR proposes that Pharmacy A wait five days to name an interim manager, and that the pharmacist simultaneously become MOR of a separate Retail Pharmacy B. Both retail stores have sufficient staffing. Which approach meets 247 CMR 9.23?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Appoint a Board-registered interim manager before the planned absence and do not concurrently serve as MOR for the second retail pharmacy.
citation: 247 CMR 9.23(3)–(5)(a),(c) (effective Dec. 6, 2024); compare 247 CMR 9.23(5)(b),(d) for unplanned absences and 100-day changes

topic: Previously dispensed medication: mandatory acceptance of defective/error returns versus restocking
question_prompt: Three people contact the SAME Massachusetts pharmacy about medications it previously dispensed. Patient X received the wrong drug. Patient Y's product is suspected to be contaminated. Patient Z received the correct, nondefective drug but no longer wants it. Assume no other specific legal return exception. Which practices follow 247 CMR 9.01? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Accept X's wrongly dispensed medication and Y's suspected defective or contaminated medication, then quarantine and properly dispose of the returned items. | The pharmacy is not required by this regulation to take back Z's properly dispensed, nondefective medication, while X's and Y's returns cannot be restocked.
citation: 247 CMR 9.01(5),(7)(a)–(b) (effective Dec. 6, 2024); distinct from 247 CMR 9.13 undelivered return-to-stock

topic: Corresponding pharmacist responsibility: authentic controlled Rx without valid patient-practitioner relationship
question_prompt: A Massachusetts community pharmacist receives an authentic Schedule IV prescription from a registered, ordinarily authorized physician. The prescriber confirms that the intended patient has never been examined, contacted, or otherwise assessed by the physician or any collaborating practitioner and that no patient–practitioner relationship was established. No standing-order, emergency, or statutory exception applies. Which response follows Massachusetts pharmacy law?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Do not dispense this prescription as described; clarify or obtain appropriate lawful prescribing care rather than rely solely on registration and authentication.
citation: 247 CMR 9.15(2)(a)–(d); 21 CFR 1306.04(a) (legitimate medical purpose and corresponding responsibility)

topic: Hydrocodone/acetaminophen rescheduling versus buprenorphine/naloxone and tramadol
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist verifies three separately issued, legitimate prescriptions: hydrocodone/acetaminophen (Vicodin), buprenorphine/naloxone (Suboxone), and tramadol (Ultram). Which federal and corresponding Massachusetts schedule assignments are correct in November 2026?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Vicodin II, Suboxone III, and tramadol IV; Massachusetts uses the same II–IV classifications through 105 CMR 700.002.
citation: 21 CFR 1308.12(b)(1)(vi) hydrocodone; 21 CFR 1308.13(e)(2) buprenorphine; 21 CFR 1308.14(b)(3) tramadol; 105 CMR 700.002(B)–(D); DEA 2014 hydrocodone combination rescheduling

topic: USP <795> default BUD distinction: preserved versus nonpreserved aqueous and nonaqueous oral liquids
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy compounds four different NONHAZARDOUS nonsterile preparations. There is no USP–NF compounded preparation monograph, formulation-specific stability study, or shorter component limitation, and all have otherwise compliant packaging. Under currently official USP <795> Section 10, which default beyond-use-date (BUD) statements are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: A nonpreserved aqueous suspension (water activity at least 0.60) generally has a maximum 14-day BUD and requires refrigerated storage. | A properly preserved aqueous CNSP generally has a 35-day maximum BUD under the stated assumptions and may be stored at controlled room temperature or refrigerated.
citation: Current USP <795> Section 10.3/Table 4 (official Nov. 1, 2023); USP General Chapter <795> 2022 Open Forum BUD slide; 247 CMR 9.01(3)

topic: Board personal-licensee profile update and changed legal name: separate 14-day compliance
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist updates a personal mailing address and telephone number, and legally changes their surname following a court order. The pharmacist's professional license is otherwise in good standing. Under 247 CMR 20.03(1)–(2), which action is required?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Update the contact details in the DPH online licensing profile within 14 calendar days and submit the required sworn name-change statement and identification within 14 calendar days.
citation: 247 CMR 20.03(1)–(2) (effective Dec. 6, 2024); Massachusetts Board Reporting Requirements Overview

topic: PDMA-marked drug samples offered to a pharmacy for repackaging and resale
question_prompt: A community pharmacy is offered manufacturer-labeled prescription samples bearing 'drug sample—not for resale.' The pharmacist proposes to use the samples to make compounded prescriptions, relabel part of the stock into ordinary pharmacy vials, and bill patients for the resulting medications. No specific exception applies. What does Massachusetts pharmacy law require?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Decline the proposal: a pharmacy may not accept or buy these samples for compounding, repacking, or resale, regardless of whether it could charge only for labor.
citation: 247 CMR 9.01(6) (effective Dec. 6, 2024); Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act §503(c)–(d), 21 U.S.C. §353(c)–(d) (PDMA sample distribution and sale)

topic: Prescription format: patient address, veterinary exemption and practitioner registration across schedules
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist reviews otherwise authentic outpatient prescriptions issued by authorized practitioners. None is a standing order, expedited partner therapy, or another special exception except the one expressly identified. Which statements about the required prescription contents under 105 CMR 721.020 are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: For an ordinary Schedule VI human prescription, the issuance date, practitioner registration number, drug identification/strength/quantity, directions, and authorized refill information remain required. | A veterinary prescription may omit the patient's name and address under the expressly listed 721.020(D)(4) exception; the other applicable veterinary and controlled-prescription requirements still apply.
citation: 105 CMR 721.020(C),(D)(1)–(6) (effective Sept. 27, 2024); DPH Elements of a Written Prescription; M.G.L. c.94C §22(a)

topic: FDA-approved Xyrem (sodium oxybate) versus unapproved gamma-hydroxybutyrate scheduling
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist compares (X) FDA-approved Xyrem (sodium oxybate), issued under all otherwise required special dispensing restrictions, with (Y) a separate unapproved gamma-hydroxybutyric acid (GHB) preparation. Which federal AND Massachusetts controlled schedules apply to these two distinct products?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Xyrem is Schedule III while unapproved GHB is Schedule I; the FDA-approved-drug-product exception does not extend to illicit or unapproved preparations.
citation: 21 CFR 1308.11(e)(6) (GHB); 21 CFR 1308.13(c)(6) (FDA-approved GHB-containing drug products); 105 CMR 700.002(A),(C); DEA Nov. 2026 GHB fact sheet

topic: Unannounced Board inspection and plan-of-correction deadlines after deficiencies
question_prompt: Massachusetts Board pharmacy inspectors visit a licensed community pharmacy without notice and cite deficiencies. The Board's written notice does not specify a shorter or longer plan-of-correction deadline. The first submitted plan is later returned as unacceptable. Under 247 CMR 9.24–9.25, which statements are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Board inspectors may make an unannounced visit and inspect staff, activities and relevant pharmacy records; the pharmacy must supply requested inspection documents. | The first written plan is due within 21 days unless the Board directs a different period, and an unacceptable plan must be revised within seven days.

topic: Pharmacy workforce: more than 12 working hours and the eight-hour consecutive rest exception
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician has already practiced in a retail pharmacy for 12 hours in the preceding 24-hour period. A last-minute staffing emergency threatens access to urgent patient prescriptions. The technician can work only 45 more minutes, and management is able to document the extenuating circumstances and minimize the extra work. Which statement most accurately applies 247 CMR 9.01(17)?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: An extenuating circumstance may permit the additional minimized, documented work in the patient's best interest; ordinarily eight consecutive hours of rest are required before resuming practice.
citation: 247 CMR 9.01(17) (effective Dec. 6, 2024); distinguish pharmacy meal-break arrangements from consecutive rest

topic: Offer to counsel versus actual counseling: trained technician and pharmacy intern
question_prompt: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy has a trained technician, a pharmacy intern and an on-duty pharmacist. The technician offers counseling to a patient with a newly prescribed drug. The patient accepts and asks how to take the drug with food and what to do after a missed dose. Under 247 CMR 9.18, who may fulfill the requested counseling?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The pharmacist or the pharmacy intern may provide the counseling; the trained technician's role may be to offer it, but not to provide clinical counseling.
citation: 247 CMR 9.18(1)–(5) (effective Dec. 6, 2024); compare 9.18(10) for inpatient practice exclusion

topic: Bedside discharge prescription delivery: patient consent, pharmacy choice and direct delivery
question_prompt: A community pharmacy offers a bedside delivery service at a Massachusetts inpatient healthcare facility for patients being discharged. A hospital discharge planner wants all patients automatically enrolled in the hospital's preferred community pharmacy, with medications dropped at the nurses' station whether or not the patient agrees. Under 247 CMR 9.04(4), which statements are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The bedside-delivery pharmacy must obtain patient consent to use the service and cannot restrict the patient's freedom to choose a pharmacy. | For a consenting patient who selects the pharmacy, the bedside service must deliver medications directly to that patient or the patient's authorized agent.
citation: 247 CMR 9.04(4) (bed-side discharge prescription delivery, effective Dec. 6, 2024); 247 CMR 9.02 not a substitute for bedside-delivery consent

topic: Vimpat lacosamide, Ketalar ketamine, and Ambien zolpidem: three distinct schedules
question_prompt: A Massachusetts community pharmacist reviews otherwise lawful prescriptions for oral lacosamide (Vimpat), ketamine (Ketalar), and zolpidem (Ambien). All products are conventional, non-exempt FDA-approved medicines. Which classification accurately states their federal and Massachusetts controlled schedules?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Vimpat Schedule V, Ketalar Schedule III, Ambien Schedule IV.

topic: USP <800> risk assessments: intact final dosage form versus manipulated antineoplastic and HD API
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy handles NIOSH-listed hazardous drugs (HDs) and considers documented assessments of risk (AOR) to use alternative containment. It receives commercially manufactured, intact Table 1 antineoplastic tablets for counting only; it also crushes a different Table 1 antineoplastic into an oral suspension, and compounds from a hazardous API. Under USP <800> and USP's January 2026 technical FAQs, which conclusions are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: A documented product- and dosage-form-specific AOR may permit alternative containment when only counting intact commercially manufactured Table 1 antineoplastic tablets, absent manufacturer instructions requiring more. | A hazardous active pharmaceutical ingredient used in compounding remains subject to full USP <800> containment requirements; a pharmacy cannot substitute a reduced-containment AOR for that API.
citation: USP <800> §§2–5 (hazardous drug list, assessment of risk and engineering controls); USP <800> FAQs updated Jan. 21, 2026, Q11–14 and Q18 (technical support, not a formal interpretation); 247 CMR 9.01(3)

topic: MOR: serious dispensing injury vs pharmacy-compounded serious adverse event
question_prompt: A resident Massachusetts pharmacy learns that an improper dispensing caused serious injury to a patient. Separately, a patient experiences a serious adverse drug event linked to a preparation compounded by that pharmacy. Under 247 CMR 20.02, which statements are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The Manager of Record must report the serious-injury improper dispensing to the Board within seven business days of discovering the injury. | The MOR must report the compounded-product serious adverse drug event to the Board, FDA MedWatch and Betsy Lehman Center.

topic: Expanded optometrist authority: ocular oral anti-infective versus opioid, systemic and injection limits
question_prompt: A Massachusetts optometrist holds the special glaucoma/ocular certification required by M.G.L. c.112 §66C and the proper state prescriptive registration. Assume every candidate prescription is authentic and all other legal conditions are met. Which proposed prescription is within this optometrist's professional scope?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: An appropriate oral anti-infective for an ocular infection being managed by the optometrist.
citation: M.G.L. c.112 §66C(a)(i)–(ii),(a)(A)–(D), effective Jan. 1, 2021; M.G.L. c.94C §7(h)

topic: Patient refusal of counseling and Massachusetts statutory documentation presumption
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist offers counseling for a new outpatient prescription. The patient clearly declines, and the pharmacist completes the necessary prospective drug review. A staff member asks whether the patient's refusal needs a record. Which interpretation follows M.G.L. c.94C §21A?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The pharmacy should reasonably record the refusal; without a recorded refusal, §21A presumes that counseling was provided.
citation: M.G.L. c.94C §21A (counseling refusal and record presumption); 247 CMR 9.18

topic: Specific schedules: testosterone cypionate, phentermine, phenobarbital
question_prompt: Which federal and corresponding Massachusetts schedules correctly classify ordinary prescription testosterone cypionate injection, phentermine capsules and phenobarbital tablets in November 2026?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Testosterone III, phentermine IV, phenobarbital IV.
citation: 21 CFR 1308.13(f)(84) (testosterone), 1308.14(c)(49) (phenobarbital), 1308.14(f)(10) (phentermine; shifted on Nov. 12, 2026); 105 CMR 700.002(C)–(D)

topic: On-site refrigerated storage: dorm unit, logs, foods and integrity assessment
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy is considering a dorm-style refrigerator with an interior freezer compartment for medicines. Management proposes storing lunches in the same refrigerator and keeping temperature excursion logs only six months. Which statements comply with 247 CMR 9.22? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The proposed dorm-style refrigerator is prohibited because its freezer compartment is within the refrigerator space. | Temperature logs must identify excursions and the pharmacy response, and must be retained for at least one year.
citation: 247 CMR 9.22(1)–(5), effective Dec. 6, 2024

topic: Annual specialty CE for temporary sterile and complex nonsterile compounding verification
question_prompt: During 2026, a Massachusetts pharmacist verifies several compounded sterile preparations and several complex nonsterile preparations during brief coverage shifts. Other approved annual CE totals 20 hours, including required law and live hours, but none concerns compounding. No Board waiver applies. What additional specialty CE compliance is necessary?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Five sterile-compounding and three complex-nonsterile-compounding CE hours in the calendar year; qualifying specialty credit may count within the general annual 20.
citation: 247 CMR 4.03(4)(c)–(d); Massachusetts Board Policy 2021-04 §§V–VII, revised Sept. 4, 2025

topic: CQI quality-related error: 24-hour documentation versus separate serious-event Board reports
question_prompt: A Massachusetts community pharmacist discovers a Quality-Related Event: a patient received the wrong prescription drug, but there is no known serious injury. The pharmacy has a CQI program. Which measures are required under 247 CMR 15? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The pharmacist must promptly address patient notification, corrective directions and measures to minimize potential harm. | Maintain QRE records for at least two years and provide pharmacy personnel with CQI education at least annually.
citation: 247 CMR 15.02(1)(f), 15.03(1)–(3), 15.04(1)–(4); 247 CMR 20.02 (separate serious-event reporting)

topic: Hospital pharmacy and on-premises hospital-owned skilled nursing residents
question_prompt: A Massachusetts hospital pharmacy wants to provide medication orders for residents of a skilled nursing facility on its premises and solely owned by the hospital. The hospital DOES NOT meet the federal criteria for a 'sole community hospital' in 42 CFR 412.92. Under 105 CMR 722.090(A), which conclusion is correct?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Ownership and location alone do not establish the specific hospital-patient exception; the owning hospital must also satisfy the referenced federal sole-community-hospital criteria.
citation: 105 CMR 722.090(A) (hospital-based SNF/LTCF exception); 42 CFR 412.92 sole community hospital

topic: DEA multiple Schedule II prescriptions versus Massachusetts 30-day original validity
question_prompt: A Massachusetts practitioner issues three separate authentic electronic prescriptions for methylphenidate on November 1, 2026, each for 30 days. The second and third give earliest-fill dates December 15 and January 15, and diversion risk and legitimate-purpose conditions are satisfied. No new prescription is issued afterward. What follows from 21 CFR 1306.12(b) and M.G.L. c.94C §23(a)?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The federal multiple-prescription option is conditional on state law, and both delayed originals would already be invalid under the Massachusetts 30-day validity limit.

topic: Emergency medication kits: reconciliation and Board-approved facility types
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy supplies emergency medication kits and proposes delivering them to any facility on request, without formal kit procedures or reconciliation against medication orders. Which statements accurately describe 247 CMR 9.09? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The pharmacy must have procedures for kit security, maintenance and use. | The pharmacy must reconcile kit use with orders and may provide kits only to Board-approved facility types.
citation: 247 CMR 9.09(1)–(3), effective Dec. 6, 2024

topic: Pharmacist license available on site, badge first name and pharmacist title, NABP e-profile
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist keeps a current Board-issued license readily available at the pharmacy but not wall-posted. The pharmacist's badge states only 'Staff Member' without a first name, and the pharmacist has no NABP e-profile number. What does 247 CMR 9.01(18)–(20) require?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Keeping the license readily available is acceptable, but the badge must show at least the pharmacist's first name and recognized pharmacist title, and an NABP e-profile is required.

topic: Licensed certified professional midwife versus APRN nurse-midwife Schedule VI limitations
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist evaluates medication orders issued by a licensed certified PROFESSIONAL midwife (not an APRN certified nurse-midwife). The professional midwife holds the required Massachusetts Controlled Substances Registration and is practicing within the officially recognized midwifery scope. Which interpretation of M.G.L. c.112 §295 is correct?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The midwife may order and administer covered Schedule VI medicines such as oxytocin and vitamin K in authorized practice, but cannot use Schedule II–V drugs under this license.
citation: M.G.L. c.112 §295(a)–(b), effective Nov. 21, 2024; 274 CMR 3.07, effective Sept. 11, 2026; M.G.L. c.94C §7(j)

topic: Massachusetts emergency interchange despite no-substitution: listed product and written buyer acceptance
question_prompt: A Massachusetts community pharmacy receives an authentic brand prescription marked 'no substitution.' The brand is unavailable during an actual medical emergency, but a less expensive drug on the Massachusetts List of Interchangeable Drugs is available. No additional restriction applies. question_prompt: A manufacturer proposes sending sealed 'Drug Sample — Not for Resale' packages by courier to a hospital pharmacy at the signed WRITTEN request of a physician licensed to prescribe the drug. The manufacturer verifies the physician's authority before shipment; a hospital recipient signs the required receipt, and the samples will be provided only under lawful practitioner sample procedures. Which assessment is most accurate?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: This hospital-practitioner sample route can be lawful, but the samples may not then become ordinary retail saleable stock or be used for pharmacy repackaging/compounding resale.
citation: 21 CFR 203.30(a)(1)–(4),(b)–(c), 203.31(a) (PDMA drug sample requests and receipts); 247 CMR 9.01(6) (sample resale/compounding/repackaging restriction)

topic: Unfilled electronic CII transfer: direct licensed-pharmacist communication and electronic annotations
question_prompt: A patient requests transfer of an UNFILLED electronic Schedule II prescription from Massachusetts retail Pharmacy A to another registered Massachusetts retail Pharmacy B. Both systems can transfer the original EPCS without altering any content. Pharmacy A instead proposes to print a PDF, email it to B's technician, and delete the old electronic record. Which procedure complies with Massachusetts Policy 2023-10 and 21 CFR 1306.08?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Transfer the intact electronic prescription directly between pharmacists and preserve the required transfer records at both sites.
citation: MA Board Policy 2023-10 I–II (Unfilled Prescriptions); 21 CFR 1306.08(e)–(h) (initial-fill EPCS transfer, documentation, retention); 247 CMR 9.14

topic: After 2026 viable-air action result: repeat EM and normal BUD restoration
question_prompt: A Massachusetts sterile-compounding pharmacy had an above-action-level VIABLE AIR result in its ISO 7 buffer room. It notified the Board and performed an RCA, appropriate remediation, CAPA and risk assessment; no nonviable particle excursion or additional Board restriction exists. The pharmacy now wants to return to ordinary beyond-use dates. Under Board Policy 2026-03, which actions are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Perform repeat environmental monitoring based on the affected ISO-classified area and action-level type; re-sample ALL sampling locations in the affected ISO area at the same time. | If proper remediation has occurred and repeat EM is below the policy's action levels, the pharmacy may resume its standard BUDs or compounding, as otherwise permitted.
citation: MA Board Policy 2026-03 §IV(A)–(C), especially IV(B)(1)–(3), Environmental Monitoring action level response (adopted September 3, 2026); USP <797> applicable EM standards

topic: Pharmacist continuing education audit: proof and retention
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist earned three hours of qualifying non-ACPE professional education 18 months ago. Those credits do NOT appear in NABP CPE Monitor, and the Board requests proof during a random CE audit. The pharmacist has only a calendar entry showing the seminar title. Which action best addresses 247 CMR 4.06 and Board Policy 2021-04?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Provide the Board the required provider, participant, program, completion-date and credit-hour evidence retained from the CE activity.
citation: 247 CMR 4.06(1)–(2) (CE completion records retained at least two years and provided on audit); Board Policy 2021-04 §I (most recent two full calendar years; non-ACPE certificate details)

topic: 42 CFR Part 2 intermediary: patient request for disclosure recipient list
question_prompt: A federally assisted Part 2 treatment program received a patient's valid written consent using a GENERAL designation for disclosures through a named intermediary. The patient now sends that intermediary a WRITTEN request for a list of recipients of identifying records disclosed under that designation in the preceding three years. Which statements accurately describe 42 CFR 2.24? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The intermediary must respond to the patient's qualifying written request within 30 days of receipt. | For disclosures within the permitted three-year lookback, the list must identify the entities receiving information, disclosure date, and a brief description of the patient-identifying information disclosed.
citation: 42 CFR 2.24(a)–(b) (specific intermediary's 30-day response and 3-year request); contrast 42 CFR 2.25 and HHS 2024 Part 2 final-rule fact sheet (accounting compliance-date caveat)

topic: Lenalidomide REMS: expired pharmacy confirmation number
question_prompt: A Lenalidomide REMS-certified pharmacy has a valid new lenalidomide prescription from a certified prescriber for an appropriately enrolled patient. All risk-category and pregnancy-test obligations have been met. The pharmacy obtained the required REMS CONFIRMATION number 26 hours ago but has not yet handed over or shipped the drug. The confirmation was not renewed. What must it do?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Do not dispense; cancel the expired confirmation number and obtain a new valid REMS confirmation before dispensing, with required counseling.
citation: FDA-approved Lenalidomide REMS Pharmacy Guide, steps 3–4: valid 24-hour pharmacy confirmation, cancellation/reissue when expired, Medication Guide; 247 CMR 9.01(21) (comply with product REMS)

topic: Massachusetts generic interchange: special container label and manufacturer
question_prompt: A Massachusetts Drug Store Pharmacy receives a brand-name tablet prescription without 'no substitution' and lawfully dispenses a LOWER-COST interchangeable generic manufactured by Company Z. The pharmacist accurately applies all routine label elements. Which additional interchange labeling follows 247 CMR 9.05(3)?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Label the product 'Interchange' or 'IC' with the actual generic name and Company Z on the container label; the originally prescribed brand may also be shown.
citation: 247 CMR 9.05(3)(a)–(e), generic/brand interchange container label and abbreviations; M.G.L. c.112 §12D (interchange authority)

topic: Hospital nursing-unit controlled-stock accountability and witnessed waste
question_prompt: A Massachusetts hospital moves bulk Schedule II–V controlled drugs from its pharmacy to an authorized nursing-unit medication cart. Its procedures are being evaluated against the Massachusetts DPH 'General accountability guidelines for controlled substances in hospitals and clinics with pharmacies.' Which measures comply? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Use a double-locked, permanently affixed cabinet or medication cart for nursing-unit Schedule II–V stock, with hard-copy or electronic perpetual inventory. | Have unused Schedule II–V portions wasted under the facility's controlled procedures by two licensed staff with co-signed documentation, unless more restrictive hospital policy applies.
citation: Massachusetts DPH General Accountability Guidelines for Controlled Substances in Hospitals and Clinics with Pharmacies, Nursing Units—General and Schedule II–V; 105 CMR 700.005 (security and accountability); 247 CMR 9.12 (separate institutional ADD)

topic: Graduating pharmacist: initial-calendar-year CE exemption versus following year's requirements
question_prompt: A pharmacist graduates from an approved PharmD program in May 2026 and obtains an active Massachusetts pharmacist license that August. They are not participating in vaccination, compounding, or CDTM activities requiring additional specialty CE. For the 2026 and 2027 calendar years, which statement correctly applies 247 CMR 4.03?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The pharmacist is CE-exempt for graduation year 2026; normal yearly requirements resume in 2027 without carryover.
citation: 247 CMR 4.03(4),(5),(8) (annual CE, no carryover and graduation-year exception); Massachusetts Board Policy 2021-04 general compliance (revised Sep. 4, 2025)

topic: MIIS pre-vaccination lookup: influenza versus zoster and COVID-19
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy offers routine adult influenza, recombinant zoster, and COVID-19 immunizations under otherwise valid standing orders. The pharmacist has current access to the Massachusetts Immunization Information System (MIIS), and the patients have no separate exemption. Under Board Policy 2023-02 revised 2025, which statements are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The policy excludes INFLUENZA vaccination from its general mandatory pre-administration MIIS lookup requirement. | For a routine recombinant ZOSTER vaccine, the pharmacy must check MIIS before administration to make sure the requested vaccination was not already administered by another provider.
citation: Board Policy 2023-02 §§IV(E)–(G), revised September 4, 2025; 105 CMR 222.100(A) (MIIS immunization reporting)

topic: 2026 Part 2 unsecured SUD-record breach notification under HIPAA-equivalent rule
question_prompt: A federally assisted substance-use-disorder treatment program subject to 42 CFR Part 2 discovers and confirms a BREACH of unsecured Part 2 patient records affecting 120 individuals. No low-probability-of-compromise finding or other exception applies. Under the Part 2 breach rule in force during November 2026, which notification plan is most accurate?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Notify patients without unreasonable delay, within 60 days, and report the under-500 breach to HHS within 60 days after year-end.
citation: 42 CFR 2.16(b) (Part 2 unsecured-record breach adopts HIPAA Breach Rule); 45 CFR 164.404(b) (individual notices), 164.408(c) (under-500 Secretary annual report); HHS OCR Part 2 breach guidance (compliance February 16, 2026)

topic: Automatic-refill program: patient enrollment consent and opt-out
question_prompt: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy wants to activate automatic monthly refills for a patient's valid Schedule VI maintenance prescription. The patient has authorized refills on file but has NEVER agreed to enroll in auto-refill. The patient later says they do not want automated fills. Which workflow follows 247 CMR 9.19(13)?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Obtain and record the patient's or agent's consent BEFORE enrollment and give the patient a way to discontinue participation; authorized refills alone do not waive either requirement.
citation: 247 CMR 9.19(13) (patient/agent recorded consent before auto-refill enrollment; discontinuation method); 247 CMR 9.04(12) (separate Schedule VI prescription validity)

topic: Workplace prescription collection and direct handoff: lawful pharmacy-agent workflow
question_prompt: A Massachusetts community pharmacy offers to collect prescriptions at a nearby factory for employees and eligible family members, then deliver completed prescriptions to the factory. It uses its own identified, authorized agents and satisfies other dispensing and counseling requirements. Under 247 CMR 9.04(9), which steps are lawful or required? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Limit the service to employees or others regularly affiliated with the location and eligible immediate family members who live at the same address as those employees or affiliates. | Have a pharmacist, pharmacy employee or authorized pharmacy agent personally collect prescriptions and dispense the medications DIRECTLY to each patient or the patient's agent.
citation: 247 CMR 9.04(9)(a)–(e) (collection at industrial plants/workplaces, eligible recipients, direct handoff and undistributed return)

topic: New staff licensure verification: pharmacy responsibility at commencement of employment
question_prompt: A Massachusetts community pharmacy hires a pharmacist and a pharmacy technician TRAINEE. HR checked both licenses eight months ago when the applicants were interviewed. On their first scheduled workday, the pharmacist's Massachusetts registration is active but the trainee license has expired. The MOR wants the trainee to prepare prescriptions while a renewal application is pending. What does 247 CMR 9.19(18) require?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Verify both workers' current Massachusetts licenses when employment commences and do not assign licensed pharmacy-technician trainee tasks to the worker whose personal license has expired.
citation: 247 CMR 9.19(18) (current licensure verification at commencement for pharmacist, intern, technician and trainee); 247 CMR 8.03 (pharmacy technician trainee licensure and scope); 247 CMR 9.04(1) (pharmacist final validation)

topic: Schedule VI prescription continuity supply after expired prescription or zero authorized refills
question_prompt: A Massachusetts patient taking a stable Schedule VI maintenance medication has an expired prescription with no remaining refills. The pharmacist has tried but cannot obtain prescriber authorization in a timely manner and has assessed that continuing therapy is appropriate. Another patient asks for the same emergency authority for Schedule IV alprazolam. No other refill, emergency or waiver provision applies. Under 247 CMR 9.04(12), which statements are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: For the Schedule VI patient, a pharmacist may exercise professional judgment to dispense a continuity quantity not exceeding 14 days OR the smallest available unit-of-use packaging in the stated circumstance. | Even though the normal one-year Schedule VI refill period has expired, the narrow continuity pathway may still apply if all its conditions are met; it is not an ordinary authorized refill.
citation: 247 CMR 9.04(12) (MA Schedule VI one-year validity and narrow 14-day/smallest-unit-of-use emergency continuity supply); compare 247 CMR 9.04(13) and 21 CFR 1306.22 for federal CIII–V

topic: Veterinarian federal Schedule III prescriptive authorization vs Schedule VI-only registration
question_prompt: A properly licensed Massachusetts veterinarian examines a dog after surgery and issues an otherwise complete patient-specific prescription for federally Schedule III buprenorphine for appropriate veterinary pain management. The veterinarian holds a Massachusetts Controlled Substance Registration (MCSR) covering Schedule VI ONLY and has NO DEA registration. The pharmacy has independently verified these facts. What should it do?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Do not dispense; Schedule III veterinary prescribing needs both appropriate DEA and Massachusetts controlled-substance authority for this animal patient.
citation: M.G.L. c.94C §§7,18(a); 105 CMR 700.004(C)–(D) (MCSR schedule authorizations); DEA 21 CFR 1306.03–1306.05; Massachusetts DPH Veterinary Prescriptions Best Practice Recommendations (January 9, 2025)

topic: MassPAT additional drug gabapentin: positive identification and hardship exception
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy dispenses prescribed gabapentin, a Massachusetts Schedule VI drug designated for PMP reporting, to an authorized patient representative at the counter. The representative has no government-issued ID. The pharmacist has credible facts showing that refusal today would cause serious hardship for the patient and can document the reason. What does 247 CMR 9.04(14) allow?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Document the serious hardship and get the agent's printed name, address and signature on the reverse of the prescription or pharmacy log before dispensing this additional drug.
citation: 247 CMR 9.04(14)(a)–(d) (positive identification for Schedules II–V and 'additional drugs', documented serious-hardship alternative); 105 CMR 700.012(A)(1) (gabapentin additional-drug reporting)

topic: Ransomware downtime: pharmacy continuity procedures, patient profiles and DUR records
question_prompt: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy discovers ransomware and disables its compromised pharmacy computer system to protect patient records. The pharmacist can still obtain reliable lawful prescriptions, consult independent medication-history sources and perform a documented prospective DUR when safe, but new dispensing transactions cannot yet be entered into the normal electronic patient profiles. Under 247 CMR 9.19(22), 9.16 and 9.17, which operational responses are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Follow a readily accessible written computer-downtime procedure that describes how prescriptions can be processed during downtime and how all medications dispensed will be entered into patient profiles when the system returns. | Protect confidentiality and use reliable alternative procedures for reviewing relevant patient history and documenting any clinical interventions; reconcile dispensing and DUR records when the system is restored.
citation: 247 CMR 9.19(22)(a)–(d) (mandatory pharmacy computer downtime plan), 9.16(1),(7) (record retention/confidential profile), 9.17(1)–(2) (prospective DUR); HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.308–312 separately governs covered electronic PHI

question_prompt: A Massachusetts prescriber telephones a retail pharmacy with a new EMERGENCY ORAL Schedule II order for a patient requiring immediate treatment. A certified technician answers, while a licensed pharmacist is on duty. The prescriber and the alleged emergency have not yet been verified. Who must assume responsibility for the oral emergency prescription record?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The licensed pharmacist should communicate with the prescriber, establish the emergency and document the oral prescription.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy intern is counseling a patient about a new inhaler. The intern's supervising pharmacist leaves for an off-site appointment during the conversation. Another pharmacist is on the premises but has not been told about the intern's task. The first pharmacist can be reached by telephone. What should happen before the consultation and dispensing are completed?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Have the on-site pharmacist take over direct supervision, actively supervise counseling, and complete final validation.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts retail pharmacist asks a currently licensed, nationally certified pharmacy technician to call a prescriber's office about a Schedule VI refill. The pharmacist has approved the call and remains responsible for clinical judgments. The receptionist can confirm the unchanged refill authorization, but the prescriber later calls back suggesting a different dose and frequency. Which actions are within the technician's role? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Ask the prescriber or authorized agent for an additional refill of the unchanged prescription and record the authorization for pharmacist review. | Relay factual information already in the patient's profile that needs no professional interpretation, while notifying the pharmacist of the suggested dose change.

question_prompt: A technician asks a patient for their current medicines, allergy history, and date of birth. An interaction alert then appears. Which actions are within the described roles? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Record the patient's factual answers in the profile for pharmacist review. | Refer the alert and any inconsistent allergy information to the pharmacist before dispensing.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist has assessed a patient's history, selected an indicated routine vaccine under a valid standing order, and personally counseled the patient. A licensed pharmacy technician who meets the Board's vaccine-administration training, experience or certification, CPR, and supervision requirements is available. A licensed pharmacy technician TRAINEE is also working. Which actions are permitted as described? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The qualified technician prepares and administers the selected vaccine under the appropriately qualified on-duty pharmacist's direct supervision. | The qualified technician administers a standing-order emergency medication for a vaccine reaction while the supervising pharmacist manages the patient.
citation: MA Board/DPH Policy 2023-02, revised Sept. 4, 2025, §§intro, III(D)(1)-(5), IV(A)-(B)

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy cashier has no pharmacy technician license and works OUTSIDE the secured prescription area. Filled, pharmacist-verified, bagged prescriptions are ready for pickup. Which actions may the cashier perform as described? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Take payment and hand over a verified bagged prescription after appropriate identity and pickup checks. | Extend the pharmacist's offer to counsel without personally giving clinical drug advice.
citation: MA Board Policy 2020-15 §I; 247 CMR 9.18(1)–(3)

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician holds an active Board-issued pharmacy technician license. The national certification that previously allowed the technician to work under the 'certified technician' category expired yesterday. A pharmacist wants the worker to continue receiving newly telephoned prescriptions and counting as a certified technician for the expanded supervisory ratio until the examination can be retaken. Which response is required?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Use ordinary technician duties, title, and ratio status until the accepted national certification is renewed.

question_prompt: During a permitted 20-minute break, the sole pharmacist remains on the pharmacy premises and the pharmacy's break procedure permits handoff only of prescriptions the pharmacist previously checked. A trained technician has entered and labeled an entirely NEW prescription, but the pharmacist has not performed prospective DUR or final validation. The patient arrives requesting immediate pickup and offers to accept a counseling call after the break. Which decision is correct?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Hold the unchecked prescription until pharmacist review.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy is providing vaccination services. One pharmacist would supervise SIX Massachusetts-licensed support personnel, all actively preparing or filling prescriptions. All applicable intern-supervision and training requirements are satisfied; there is no waiver or dedicated trainer. Which roster qualifies for the Board's vaccination-service 1:6 ratio?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: One certified technician, two pharmacy interns, and three noncertified technicians.
citation: MA Board Policy 2026-02 §I(B)(1)–(2), adopted September 3, 2026

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist has a FOUR-person prescription-filling team: two licensed certified technicians, one licensed noncertified technician, and one licensed technician trainee. An additional licensed certified technician is excluded from the supervisory ratio as a designated dedicated trainer who only oversees that trainee. Mid-shift, the trainer begins independently filling prescriptions for other patients while continuing to train. No vaccination exception or waiver applies. What must change?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Count the trainer while independently filling prescriptions; adjust staffing or duties to restore a compliant ratio.
citation: MA Board Policy 2026-02 §§I(A), III(A)(1)(c), III(A)(2)(c), III(B)

question_prompt: One Massachusetts pharmacist preceptor supervises FOUR licensed interns at a simulated medication-workflow workshop OUTSIDE any pharmacy. No real prescriptions or patient consultations occur. In the afternoon, all four will move into a hospital pharmacy and begin preparing actual patient prescriptions, still under that one preceptor. No waiver or second pharmacist applies. Which change is required?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Restrict the real prescription-filling work to two interns per preceptor, or add another qualified preceptor.
citation: 247 CMR 8.01(16); Board Policy 2026-02 §II(A)–(C)

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy intern with a current intern license completes 9 supervised hours at Pharmacy A on a Monday and 5 supervised hours at Pharmacy B later that same Monday. Both preceptors document the actual work and all other supervision requirements are satisfied. The intern asks to submit all 14 hours for Board internship credit because no individual employer assigned more than 12. What is the maximum credit that may be claimed for that calendar day?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Count no more than twelve hours of approved internship credit for that day, across both pharmacy locations.
citation: 247 CMR 8.01(3)–(5) (current intern hours limitation)

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist has three years of licensed experience, completed an accredited clinical residency, and wants to enter a CDTM agreement. The pharmacist has no pre-July 2017 PharmD agreement. Who must determine whether the residency substitutes for five years of experience?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The Board, under its education-or-residency equivalency pathway.

question_prompt: An otherwise qualified Massachusetts pharmacist plans to sign a two-year CDTM agreement on November 20, 2026. The pharmacist's employer provides liability coverage, but the certificate lists only routine dispensing activities and says nothing about drug therapy management. The coverage is $2 million per occurrence and remains active. Which change is necessary before the pharmacist qualifies under 247 CMR 16.02?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Require qualifying liability coverage of at least $1 million per occurrence specifically for CDTM throughout the agreement term.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts COMMUNITY pharmacist has a valid physician CDTM agreement, written patient referral and consent for diabetes care, Massachusetts prescribing registration, and a personal DEA registration. The collaborating physician wants the pharmacist to begin prescribing Schedule IV alprazolam under the same community CDTM agreement. What is the legal result?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Community CDTM forbids prescribing Schedule II–V medicines, even with a personal DEA registration.

question_prompt: A pharmacist maintains a valid Massachusetts CDTM agreement to co-manage adults' diabetes therapy. During a particular year of the agreement, the pharmacist completes 20 Board-approved CE contact hours needed for ordinary renewal, but none of the activities relate generally to the CDTM diabetes practice area. The pharmacist asks whether the ordinary renewal hours alone satisfy CDTM maintenance. What is correct?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Complete at least five additional approved CE contact hours in the related CDTM practice area each agreement year.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist was unable to complete several required continuing-education hours because of a documented serious illness. The pharmacist requests consideration of extenuating circumstances and submits a signed, detailed statement with the renewal application. Who determines whether renewal can be granted under 247 CMR 4.03(6)?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The Board, after considering the signed, detailed explanation.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist graduated from an approved pharmacy school in May 2025, obtained a Massachusetts license later in 2025, and is preparing CE records for the calendar years 2025 and 2026. The pharmacist worked in routine retail dispensing, with no sterile or complex compounding. Assume no Board-granted exception. Which interpretation follows 247 CMR 4.03?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The graduation-year exemption covers 2025; the normal annual CE minimum applies in calendar year 2026, without carryover.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist who neither compounds nor vaccinates reports precisely 20 CE hours in calendar year 2026: 16 hours of mediated/home study and 4 hours live, including two pharmacy-law hours. All sessions are approved, but nine CE hours were earned on one single calendar day; remaining hours were on compliant days. Does this satisfy the 2026 minimum?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: No; only 15 mediated plus four live CE hours may count, leaving fewer than 20 hours for the year.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts-licensed pharmacy intern changes the address and email in the intern's personal life and, separately, changes the legal name after marriage. The intern tells the pharmacy manager and corrects the employer's HR payroll file on the day of the changes. Under the Board's current general reporting rules, which further actions are required? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Update the intern's own Massachusetts DPH online licensing profile with the new mailing address and email within 14 calendar days. | Submit the required sworn name-change statement with valid photo identification and any other Board-requested documents within 14 calendar days.

question_prompt: A pharmacist reports taking a lawfully prescribed sedative, but on this shift is visibly confused and repeatedly selects the wrong product. Which action best addresses the immediate pharmacy-law concern?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Stop unsafe dispensing and arrange appropriate coverage while the impairment is evaluated.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist has a current unrestricted registration, has applied to a voluntary monitoring program for a possible substance-use problem, and is waiting for admission. The Board has NOT issued an order limiting practice. A second pharmacist has a CURRENT registration but is bound by a Board order prohibiting controlled-substance handling; that pharmacist has also applied to monitoring and assumes the order is automatically suspended. Which statement BEST reflects 247 CMR 10.03?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Comply with the active Board restrictions; a pending monitoring application does not remove them or excuse impaired practice.
citation: 247 CMR 10.03(1)(g),(i),(j); 247 CMR 16.02(3) where CDTM applies

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist is arrested on Monday, May 4, 2026. A separate state licensing board then imposes a FINAL disciplinary restriction on the pharmacist on Wednesday, May 6. The pharmacist submits the required notices to the Massachusetts Board on Monday, May 18. Assume the Board receives them that day and no holidays affect the business-day count. Which assessment of the reporting deadlines is correct?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The arrest notice meets the fourteen-calendar-day rule, but the other state's final disciplinary action missed the seven-business-day reporting deadline.
citation: 247 CMR 20.03(3)–(4) (14-calendar-day notices); 247 CMR 10.03(1)(z) (7-business-day notice for final out-of-state action)

question_prompt: ed pharmacy technician also holds a Board-accepted national certification. On November 4, 2026, the technician's certifying body permanently revokes that national certification after its own disciplinary proceeding. Separately, on November 5, the licensed pharmacy receives written notice that its accreditation status has been adversely changed. The technician's Massachusetts state license and the pharmacy's license have not yet been suspended. Which reporting conclusions follow 247 CMR 20.03? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The technician's loss of certification is a reporting trigger even though the Massachusetts technician license is still active. | The pharmacy's adverse change of accreditation must be reported to the Board within 14 calendar days.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy-technician applicant truthfully discloses an old misdemeanor unrelated to drugs, with no drug-related felony conviction or admission to sufficient facts. Which conclusion follows from 247 CMR 8.02?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The drug-felony bar is not shown; other licensing requirements still apply.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy has three people scheduled to perform pharmacist duties. One holds a current unrestricted Massachusetts pharmacist registration. Another is licensed but subject to a current Board order prohibiting controlled-substance handling. The third pharmacist's registration expired yesterday and renewal is pending. Who can be assigned final validation for a Schedule II prescription, assuming all normal reviews are performed?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The pharmacist with an active, unrestricted Massachusetts license, who completes all required reviews.

question_prompt: A physician resident without an individual DEA registration works in a Massachusetts hospital. The resident is licensed or otherwise authorized to prescribe in the hospital's state-authorized practice, and the DEA-registered hospital has assigned the resident a unique internal identifier for prescriptions using its institutional DEA number. A patient later visits the resident at an UNRELATED private office where the resident has no institutional authorization. Which use of DEA identifiers is correct?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Use the hospital's DEA number and assigned suffix for authorized hospital practice, not at an unrelated private office.
citation: 21 CFR 1301.22(c)(1)–(6); 21 CFR 1306.05; MA applicable prescriptive authority

question_prompt: A physician serving as a properly authorized U.S. Public Health Service officer writes a legitimate Schedule IV prescription while performing assigned federal duties at a qualifying federal clinic. The physician uses the permitted agency/service identifier instead of an individual DEA registration. On weekends, the same physician operates a private medical practice in Massachusetts and wishes to use that exemption for private controlled-substance prescriptions. Which conclusion is correct?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The federal exemption can cover official PHS duties, but unrelated private prescribing requires appropriate DEA and state authority.

question_prompt: achusetts retail pharmacy receives an otherwise valid electronic prescription for methylphenidate (Ritalin immediate-release) for a local patient. It was issued four days ago by a properly licensed, DEA-registered prescriber practicing in California. The patient has a genuine patient-practitioner relationship, and the pharmacist verifies authenticity and medical legitimacy directly with the prescriber's office. The pharmacy is not conducting mail-order dispensing. Which Massachusetts-specific conclusion is correct?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: It may be filled if all requirements are met, with the statutory department report.
citation: M.G.L. c.94C §18(d) (nonnarcotic out-of-state Schedule II; issuance, verification, reporting)

question_prompt: A licensed Massachusetts nurse practitioner issues an otherwise valid Schedule IV prescription. The electronic record contains the NP's name, credentials, MCSR and DEA number but omits a supervising practitioner's name. The pharmacist verifies through reliable licensure and prescribing-authority information that the NP has completed the required supervised practice and has amended the MCSR for INDEPENDENT prescriptive practice. What is the appropriate conclusion about the missing supervisor's name?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: A verified independent NP prescription need not list a supervising clinician's name; other controlled-Rx requirements still apply.
citation: 105 CMR 721.020(E); M.G.L. c.112 §80E; MA DPH APRN prescribing authority guidance

question_prompt: A Massachusetts physician assistant has a CURRENT TEMPORARY PA license but has not passed the national certification examination for full licensure. At a clinic, the PA prepares a Schedule VI written prescription for a patient. The supervising physician reviews and personally SIGNS it before issuance and it is issued in that physician's name. Assume the physician has prescribing authority, the PA's temporary work is otherwise authorized, and all remaining prescription elements are valid. Which statement is correct?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: This may meet the temporary-PA pathway because the supervising physician signs before issuance and the order is in that physician's name.
citation: 263 CMR 5.06(2)(a)–(c) (temporary PA prescriptive order); M.G.L. c.94C §7

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist evaluates otherwise authentic prescriptions with appropriate registration identifiers. question_prompt: h the required state and federal controlled-substance prescribing authority conducts a real-time two-way AUDIO-VIDEO telemedicine visit with an adult patient located in Massachusetts in November 2026. question_prompt: A Massachusetts clinic issues a new Schedule IV prescription using electronic prescribing of controlled substances (EPCS). question_prompt: scriber telephones a community pharmacist seeking a new Schedule II oral prescription for a patient in acute distress. question_prompt: On November 1, 2026, an authorized Massachusetts practitioner signs and issues two separate electronic Schedule II prescriptions for a legitimate 28-day course. Office staff propose changing the second issue date to November 15, even though the practitioner actually signed it November 1. Which procedure is correct?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Keep November 1 as the genuine issue date and November 15 as the earliest fill date, then check state-law validity before dispensing.

question_prompt: A prescriber wants to give a 15-year-old an initial 10-day outpatient opioid prescription for a documented acute condition. Which additional action supports the statutory exception to the usual seven-day limit?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Document the qualifying condition and why non-opiate treatment is inappropriate.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy ships a patient's NEW outpatient prescription to the patient's home at the patient's election. question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy's authorized pickup agent collects a NEW prescription for a patient who is not at the store. The pharmacy offers access to pharmacist counseling, and the agent says: 'The patient asked me to pick this up, but I did not ask whether she wants counseling.' The cashier proposes recording 'patient refused counseling' solely on that statement. What is the most appropriate response?

topic: Offer, later refusal and counseling record
question_prompt: At a Massachusetts community pharmacy, a properly trained technician offers pharmacist counseling for a new oral prescription. The staff record says 'Counseling completed.' Which conclusions are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

question_prompt: A deaf patient who primarily uses American Sign Language arrives alone at a Massachusetts retail pharmacy for an important first-dose anticoagulant counseling visit. question_prompt: Massachusetts pharmacy is asked to send a patient's ordinary prescription history to the physician managing that patient's current treatment. The physician identifies the patient and describes the clinical purpose. No special confidentiality statute or patient's authorization has been provided for the organizer. Which HIPAA statements are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

question_prompt: A 16-year-old lawfully consents in Massachusetts to treatment for an eligible confidential medical service under M.G.L. c.112 §12F. The dispensing pharmacy is subject to HIPAA. A parent who is not authorized by the minor requests the entire pharmacy record for that episode, saying, 'I am the parent, so HIPAA always makes me the personal representative.' No court order, emergency, or other exception is stated. What is the BEST initial response?

citation: 45 CFR 164.502(g)(3)(i)–(ii) (HIPAA minor as personal representative exception); M.G.L. c.112 §12F (MA minor self-consent; physician/dentist record clause is limited)

question_prompt: A HIPAA-covered Massachusetts pharmacy receives a patient's records from a federally assisted substance-use-disorder program subject to 42 CFR Part 2, pursuant to valid general written TPO consent. A claims reviewer needs the records for ordinary payment operations. Separately, an attorney sends a subpoena seeking to use the same records AGAINST THE PATIENT in a civil proceeding; no additional patient consent or Part 2-qualified court order exists. Which conclusions are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

citation: 42 CFR 2.31, 2.33, 2.63–2.67 (2026 compliance); HHS Part 2 guidance

question_prompt: ts community pharmacist has a current asthma CDTM agreement with supervising physician Dr. Q. The physician supplied a valid referral and written patient consent; the written protocol authorizes adjustments ONLY to asthma medications Dr. Q has prescribed. The patient brings an inhaler prescribed instead by unrelated pulmonologist Dr. P and asks the pharmacist to change its dose. Dr. Q has not prescribed or otherwise authorized this inhaler, and no separate prescribing pathway applies. What should the pharmacist do?

question_prompt: il pharmacist participates in a currently signed community CDTM agreement focused on diabetes. No physician has amended the referral or the defined scope of the agreement. What is the best action?

question_prompt: a current collaborative drug therapy management (CDTM) agreement. A supervising physician has referred an adult patient for DIABETES medication management, obtained the patient's written consent, and approved a protocol allowing drug-related laboratory monitoring under physician supervision or direct consultation. The patient now asks the pharmacist to order an unrelated diagnostic test to investigate unexplained abdominal pain. No other prescribing or diagnostic authority is established. What is most appropriate?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Continue approved diabetes-drug monitoring under physician oversight; refer the unrelated diagnostic workup to a clinician.
citation: 247 CMR 16.03(5)(c)–(e) (community CDTM referral/consent, eligible diabetes therapy); 243 CMR 2.12(1) (protocol-linked nondiagnostic monitoring); 247 CMR 16.04(2)

question_prompt: A pharmacist with a current community-pharmacy CDTM agreement has a physician referral and consent for an adult's diabetes medication management. At 8:00 a.m. the pharmacist makes a permitted Schedule VI dose adjustment under the protocol; later a new critical finding indicates urgent physician review is needed. The pharmacist documents the medication action but plans to tell the physician only at the next monthly visit. What is required?
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Notify the physician within 24 hours, escalate urgent findings sooner, and document the change in the patient record.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts patient originally gave written informed consent for the community pharmacy's diabetes CDTM program and had a patient-specific physician referral. The pharmacist and physician's general collaborative agreement remains active. Today the patient expressly withdraws consent for THIS patient-specific collaboration while asking the pharmacist to manage diabetes medication doses without involving the physician. existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Document the patient's withdrawal, stop CDTM dose changes for that patient, and arrange care through an authorized prescriber.

question_prompt: tem operates both a Massachusetts licensed hospital and an independently licensed community pharmacy. SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts community pharmacy has a valid standing order for routine vaccines. A properly qualified pharmacist and intern have current CPR and immunization credentials. Two siblings, one aged 4 years 11 months and one aged exactly 5 years, arrive with their guardian. question_prompt: A qualified Massachusetts pharmacist is about to administer an indicated RECOMBINANT ZOSTER vaccine. question_prompt: In November 2026, an adult Massachusetts patient asks a qualified pharmacist to issue a NEW pharmacist-origin hormonal contraceptive prescription under M.G.L. c.94C §19F. question_prompt: A patient aged 28 years with an established HIV-prevention treatment plan brings a valid prescription for single-dose intramuscular cabotegravir to a Massachusetts retail pharmacy. question_prompt: In Massachusetts, a prescriber treats a patient for chlamydia and issues a second valid, signed partner-treatment prescription marked 'EPT' because the unexamined partner's name is unknown.
