question_prompt: A technician discovers a wrong-strength label while checking a prescription, before it is handed to any patient or representative. citation: 247 CMR 15.01 definition of Quality Related Event; 247 CMR 15.02(1)

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy performs final validation on a prescription and detects the wrong tablet strength BEFORE the medication leaves the prescription area. The error is corrected and the patient receives the correct product. A week later, another wrong-strength prescription is actually dispensed and received by a patient, and the pharmacist learns of it at 2:00 p.m. Wednesday. citation: MA Board Policy 2025-02 §II(F) (QRE definition); 247 CMR 15.03(1)–(2) (response and initial record)

question_prompt: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy stores its QRE event records in a secure centralized cloud system but has NO written CQI program description available at the pharmacy itself. existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Retain the written CQI program at the pharmacy and keep off-site QRE records securely accessible to the staff.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy has completed the immediate patient notifications and initial reports for several unrelated wrong-strength dispensing events. Under 247 CMR 15.02–15.03, which further responses belong in an appropriate CQI program? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Communicate adopted workflow/process changes to the affected pharmacy personnel and include CQI education at least annually. | Aggregate and examine the events for workflow, technology, training and staffing contributors instead of treating each event only as isolated blame. | Develop a measurable follow-up indicator and evaluate whether proposed workflow changes reduce errors over an identified period.

question_prompt: A patient who can get pregnant was enrolled for isotretinoin treatment and had the required pre-treatment pregnancy testing. A pharmacy technician says the patient must still wait under an older REMS rule and could simply send an at-home test photo. question_prompt: A Massachusetts REMS-certified retail pharmacy receives an otherwise valid new lenalidomide prescription from a certified prescriber. question_prompt: ssachusetts pharmacist receives an authorized emergency ORAL Schedule II prescription at 9:00 a.m. Monday for 30 tablets, an appropriate emergency-period quantity. What should the pharmacist do?

question_prompt: orphine prescription for an adult Massachusetts patient living in a licensed LONG-TERM CARE FACILITY. existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: The remaining 60 tablets may complete the original Schedule IV partial quantity without automatically consuming the separate refill.

existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Verify the record and authorization; separately assess lawful continuity options.

question_prompt: setts receives a patient's new EPCS Schedule II prescription, enters it into the computer, adjudicates an insurance claim and prints a pharmacy label. existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Confirm whether any medication was actually dispensed; if not, use the valid original EPCS transfer process.
citation: 21 CFR 1306.08(e)–(h); MA Board Policy 2023-10 (Unfilled Prescriptions)

question_prompt: Three Massachusetts pharmacies are involved in otherwise valid Schedule IV refill transfers. existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Permit the outside transfer only if the federal one-time allowance is unused and Massachusetts rules are satisfied.

question_prompt: is manually documenting a Schedule IV refill transfer discussed directly with the pharmacist at the old location. question_prompt: A Massachusetts patient has an electronic Schedule II prescription for 40 tablets. question_prompt: A patient received a TEN-DAY Schedule VI medication supply from a Massachusetts hospital pharmacy while being discharged after surgery, pursuant to its discharge-dispensing authority. existing_keyed_conclusion_UNVERIFIED: Obtain a new lawful retail order from an authorized prescriber; the hospital's discharge label is not itself a refill authorization.

question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacist receives a new otherwise legitimate Schedule II prescription that has the proper prescriber's signature but OMITS the prescriber's DEA registration number. question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy dispenses Neurontin (gabapentin). A clerk claims no MassPAT report is needed because federal DEA does not schedule this drug. Which classification and reporting statement is correct?

question_prompt: A Massachusetts veterinarian issues a valid outpatient MASSACHUSETTS SCHEDULE VI controlled-substance prescription for a cat's medication. question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy compounds a patient-specific NONSTERILE topical preparation with a supported assigned BUD of 21 days and a required refrigeration condition. question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy prepares a 30-day multi-drug-single-dose package containing two compatible Schedule VI tablets and one compatible Schedule IV maintenance tablet. topic: Prescriber PPPA packaging instruction after transfer
question_prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives a lawful transfer of the remaining refills of a prescription for an oral medicine subject to federal child-resistant packaging requirements. question_prompt: A sealed bottle's actual tablets meet specifications, but the manufacturer's label contains a materially false therapeutic claim. Which federal category is established by the false label itself?
